subject: Vendor portal account consolidation & role-mapping proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor portal account consolidation & role-mapping proposal

Tom —

Thanks again for walking through your onboarding checklist last week. To reduce friction going forward we've put together a proposal to consolidate your team’s vendor portal access (Whistic, Vendr, OneTrust and Archer) behind a single SSO + SCIM provisioning flow and formalize role mappings and evidence TTLs. High-level asks:

- Confirm PulseHealth’s preferred IdP (Okta / Azure AD / Ping).
- Confirm whether you want Redwood service accounts to be centrally managed (we rotate keys) or to keep PulseHealth-managed service accounts.
- Review the attached portal-role-matrix.xlsx and service-account-inventory.csv for suggested mappings and owners.

Proposed outcome: one SSO app + SCIM to provision accounts in portals, three roles (Owner, Reviewer, Read-only auditor), and automated evidence reminders by TTL. That reduces duplicate accounts and clarifies who owns each piece of evidence in each portal.

If this direction looks sensible, can you share a couple of 30-minute windows this week for a short technical sync? I’ve cc’d Kimberly and Ben to iron out retention and secret rotation details.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Integrations, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

Attachments: portal-role-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), service-account-inventory.csv (csv)
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@pulsehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: PulseHealth InfoSec <infosec@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor portal account consolidation & role-mapping proposal

Karthik —

Appreciate the clear proposal. A few clarifying questions from our side before we sync:

- Delegated access: will Owners be able to see all evidence across our org or only for their scoped business units? We need strict scoping for PHI-bearing teams.
- Audit trail: can you guarantee portal-level audit logs show SCIM provisioning events and which service account performed them?
- Service account rotation: if Redwood rotates keys, how do you ensure existing OIDC/robot accounts in our pipelines aren’t impacted?

One more ask — can you call out the default TTL you propose for evidence and whether that’s configurable per-control type?

I can do a sync tomorrow at 11:00am PT.

Thanks,
Tom Hayes
Security Engineering Manager, PulseHealth

On Tue, Apr 6, 2027 at 09:14 AM Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@pulsehealth.com> wrote:
> Karthik —
> 
> Appreciate the clear proposal. A few clarifying questions from our side before we sync:
> 
> - Delegated access: will Owners be able to see all evidence across our org or only for their scoped business units? We need strict scoping for PHI-bearing teams.
> - Audit trail: can you guarantee portal-level audit logs show SCIM provisioning events and which service account performed them?
> - Service account rotation: if Redwood rotates keys, how do you ensure existing OIDC/robot accounts in our pipelines aren’t impacted?
> 
> One more ask — can you call out the default TTL you propose for evidence and whether that’s configurable per-control type?

Good questions — here’s how we recommend proceeding (short version):

- Scoping: Owners are assigned at the business-unit level in the role matrix; Owners see evidence for their BU only. We’ll add an "auditor" role with org-wide read-only visibility for your compliance team.
- Audit trail: All SCIM provisioning and role changes go to our audit stream (we push events to your SIEM via webhook) and portals retain native provisioning logs — we will provide the log mapping during the sync.
- Service accounts: two supported patterns — (A) PulseHealth-managed service accounts: you keep secrets in your vault; we provide instructions for rotation and a no-downtime rotation process, or (B) Redwood-managed service accounts where we rotate keys and publish rotation events to your webhook. We recommend A for CI consumers and B for API-based bulk evidence uploads.
- TTLs: default proposal is 12 months for organizational policies and 9-12 months for technical infra controls. TTL is configurable per-control in the matrix; we'll surface a per-control banner in the console and send scheduled reminders 30/15/7 days before expiry.

I attached a short TTL-policy-draft.md and updated the role matrix to reflect per-BU Owner assignments. If Kimberly signs off on the retention buckets I’ll send a draft SCIM attribute-schema and an Okta app manifest for review.

Proposed sync: Wed Apr 7, 11:00am PT (Tom confirmed slot).

—Karthik

> - Scoping: Owners are assigned at the business-unit level in the role matrix; Owners see evidence for their BU only. We’ll add an "auditor" role with org-wide read-only visibility for your compliance team.
> - Audit trail: All SCIM provisioning and role changes go to our audit stream (we push events to your SIEM via webhook) and portals retain native provisioning logs — we will provide the log mapping during the sync.
> - Service accounts: two supported patterns — (A) PulseHealth-managed service accounts: you keep secrets in your vault; we provide instructions for rotation and a no-downtime rotation process, or (B) Redwood-managed service accounts where we rotate keys and publish rotation events to your webhook. We recommend A for CI consumers and B for API-based bulk evidence uploads.
> - TTLs: default proposal is 12 months for organizational policies and 9-12 months for technical infra controls. TTL is configurable per-control in the matrix; we'll surface a per-control banner in the console and send scheduled reminders 30/15/7 days before expiry.

Thanks — this captures our security bar. I have two adjustments before we present to PulseHealth:

1) Evidence TTL: set infra controls to 9 months and org/process controls to 12 months. Add an exception process for data classification-related controls (PHI) requiring quarterly refresh.
2) Add a distinct "Read-only auditor" persona (no ability to upload or edit evidence) and a "Break-glass admin" flag for one individual per BU; break-glass activations must be logged and emailed to a distribution list.

Also: ensure all vault rotations write a rotation-event to our audit webhook so we have linkage between secret rotations and provisioning events. Once Ben updates the matrix I approve and will loop Legal for the PO/contract clause on SCIM/SCIM-deprovisioning SLA.

Kimberly Park
Security Operations Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.ai
